title: Iron follows the hills
changes: Fresh worlds place eight finite Iron deposits in three connected hill districts, instead of giving every capital an owned deposit. Revealed outcrops follow the actual sites and show remaining reserves.

Two capitals have structural approaches to the deposits, not free access or promised income. Land purchase, Mine work and later Foundry production still need their separate costs, people and supplies.

title: A crew for unfinished civic work
changes: Civilizations with State workforce may commission three actual Kiln staff for two scheduled seasons of paid work on one existing building order, instead of ordinary Kiln production.

Each successful season pays 1 Material and 2 Credits for capped extra construction work. Existing supplies and paid work stay protected; blocked work leaves ordinary operation available, and the commission expires without an automatic follow-on.

title: Coastal opportunities, local costs
changes: Civilizations assess actual shore towns, ocean paths and available settlement sites before investing in a Boat yard or favoring Navigation. Existing research and paid construction continue independently.

Coastal departures protect current supplies, home workers and household needs. Global first-coast bonuses no longer override ordinary town limits; a useful local prospect does not guarantee a later settlement or era change.
